source.title: A Probabilistic Representation of DNNs: Bridging Mutual Information and Generalization

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures mutual information and generalization error in MLPs to test whether the information measure predicts generalization; it does not test the specific behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 5 reports average generalization error for six MLPs on two datasets across epochs. The paper also compares MI bounds, but those bound values are not outcomes for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares mutual-information bounds with training–test accuracy gaps across MLP architectures. These results test none of V1–V8. In particular, varying width does not test V2: the paper reports gaps rather than test error and does not establish the width needed for zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim their probabilistic representation permits direct mutual-information estimation, validates an information-theoretic explanation of generalization, and produces tighter bounds than the compared relaxations. Their experiments concern six MLPs on synthetic data and Fashion-MNIST; extending the approach to CNNs is future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies an MI estimator and its relationship to generalization error, rather than the claim's memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares results across synthetic and FMNIST datasets and MLP architectures; the plotted outcomes vary across epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 reports that larger MLPs learn more estimated mutual information and show larger training–test accuracy gaps in Figure 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the tested synthetic-data and Fashion-MNIST MLP architectures, estimated training-sample mutual information tracks the training–test accuracy gap.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the ICML 2021 Workshop on Theoretic Foundation, Criticism, and Application Trend of Explainable AI
record.problems: The generalization-error comparisons are presented as plots without numeric values in the text. The paper reports averaging over 100 random initializations but gives no uncertainty estimates for these plotted results.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. MI estimates and MI-bound comparisons were omitted because they do not themselves measure the behaviors named in the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied Figure 5 text contains axes and legends but does not preserve readable curve values. None of the rows supports a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Test error after widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers' held-out performance.
Large versus small batch sizes and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
